text: Chapter one was about what to draw and why. Now we learn to draw it. matplotlib is the foundation of Python plotting: seaborn is built on it, and pandas' dot plot calls it. Learn its model once and every other library gets easier.

Two core objects. A Figure is the whole canvas, the sheet of paper you can save as an image. An Axes is one plot on that canvas; it owns the x-axis, the y-axis, the title, and the data. plt dot subplots creates a figure and an axes together and returns both.

You'll see two styles in tutorials. Pyplot style is quick and implicit, relying on matplotlib remembering which axes is current. Object-oriented style is explicit: fig, ax equals plt dot subplots, then ax dot plot, ax dot set_title. We use the object-oriented style for the rest of the course.

Here's a line chart of illustrative monthly revenue, climbing from one hundred thousand dollars in January to one hundred forty-five point eight thousand in December, with a dip in September. marker equals o puts a dot on each point, and fig dot autofmt_xdate rotates crowded date labels so they don't overlap.

Every chart type is a method on the axes, same pattern every time: create the axes, call a method, add labels. Bar and barh compare categories. Hist shows a distribution. Scatter shows a relationship, with s setting marker area. Boxplot compares the spread of several groups at once.

To save a figure, call fig dot savefig with a filename. dpi equals one thirty or higher controls resolution, three hundred is common for print. bbox_inches equals tight trims extra whitespace. The file extension picks the format: PNG for slides and web, SVG or PDF for vector graphics.

A Figure is the canvas, an Axes is one plot on it, and five methods, plot, bar, barh, hist, scatter and boxplot, cover most exploratory charts. Next lesson: customizing charts with colors, styles, annotations and legends.
